title: Tilbury Bank partner scouting jot
content:
Context: Tilbury Bank — regional mid-market bank (UK based), digital transformation push, running a small "embedded intelligence" team. Heard from intro call (Nov) that payments reconciliation and customer support automation are highest priority. They are sensitive to vendor lock-in and need on-prem / VPC options and strong audit trails for compliance (FCA).

Key contacts (notes):
- Hannah Brooks (Head of Digital, +44) — champion, cares about operational reliability and data residency.
- Samir Kapoor (Lead Engineering) — skeptical about latency and model drift, mentions legacy mainframe connectors.
- Priya Nair (Compliance) — will require KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.

Quick account thesis: Tilbury will adopt tech if we can show predictable per-request latency <200ms p95 for common flows, a safe fallback strategy for peak times, and an on-prem/private deployment plan that fits their CD/CI needs. Value props to highlight: dedicated capacity (predictable throughput), KV caching to speed common queries, and Redwood Optimize recommendations to lower unit costs without degrading answers.

Pain / contraints listed by contact:
- Strict data residency + encryption in transit + audit retention 7 years
- Heavy tail of unpredictable nightly batch jobs that spike API demand
- Existing support team expects tool to hand back evidence that a decision was machine-assisted (traceability)

Draft outbound sequence (short):
1) Quick intro email (2–3 lines): connect Hannah, one pager link, propose 20m to show latency snapshot and a privacy architecture sketch.
2) Follow-up with two screenshots: Console per-route latency, a snippet of rollout policy for fallback.
3) Technical outreach to Samir: short checklist of connectors, suggested artifact: small PoC plan (2 weeks, private deploy, single endpoint).

Objections and suggested replies (brainstorm):
- "We can't have production data leave our network." -> "We offer Private with a customer-controlled control plane and on-prem option; we can run an initial PoC in your VPC and provide SOC2/KMS integration checklist up front."
- "Latency won't meet our SLOs at scale." -> "We can pre-run a load profile using one of our verified models on a dedicated pool and share token-level latency histograms; KV caching + batching typically cuts p95 by ~30–50% for their query mix."
- "Model hallucinations / compliance risk." -> "Tie responses to provenance: structured outputs + function calling + configurable guardrails; show our eval run on a sample prompt set with regression alerts enabled."

POC sketch (2-week):
Week 0: scope + account access (VPN cert or temp VPC peering)
Week 1: deploy private control plane + one model endpoint, run synthetic traffic mirrored to their workload, capture latency/cost metrics
Week 2: integrate one support flow (reconciliation Q&A) with KV cache and simple reranking; handoff runbook + cost forecast

Open questions / todo:
- Need to confirm whether Tilbury can accept our standard on-prem license (legal). TODO: loop in legal for a redline.
- Which branch of their mainframe adapter will we need access to? Samir to share.
- Prepare short demo dataset (sanitized) for compliance to sign off on PoC.

Notes to self: keep the first email tightly focused on reliability and privacy; defer cost conversation until after we show latency and a simple price model. Avoid jargon in initial thread — use specific SLO numbers and a visual (latency histogram).

Next steps:
- Draft intro email for Leila -> Hannah (Owen to review) by EOD Fri
- Request legal intake for on-prem license by next Tues
- Build a 1-page architecture diagram for private deployment (Marco)

Scratch ends.
